summary: Payer manuals and dispute policies read from the payers' own sites (Humana, Anthem KY/IN commercial, MA and Medicaid, UnitedHealthcare incl. UMR, Cigna, Humana/Anthem/WellCare/Aetna KY Medicaid, Anthem/MHS/CareSource IN Medicaid). The real, citable leverage in them is: (1) the payer's own published response times (Humana KY Medicaid, Anthem KY Medicaid, Aetna KY: 30 days; Anthem MA: 'every effort' 45 days reconsideration / 30 days appeal; Cigna: 60-day review, notice within 75 business days; Humana escalations: acknowledgment in 5 business days, response in 30-45 days); (2) deemed approval in Indiana Medicaid: Anthem IN, MHS and CareSource each state that if the formal appeal is not decided within 45 days it is decided for the provider; (3) next-step rights that must be preserved by a deadline or are lost: UHC Notice of Dispute within 60 days of the appeal decision or waiver 'in any forum'; Anthem commercial appeal within 90 days of the reconsideration; Cigna arbitration within 1 year; MHS pre-arbitration within 60 days; Kentucky Medicaid external independent review within 60 days; (4) Kentucky Medicaid's in-person meeting right for claims unpaid 45+ days over $2,500 individually or in aggregate (Humana, Anthem and Aetna KY manuals), which rewards pooling small balances. Filing windows for contracted commercial/MA disputes are long (Humana 18 months; Anthem KY/IN commercial 2 years then 90 days; UHC 12 months for both steps; Cigna 180 days; WellCare KY 24 months; Humana KY contract-rate disputes 24 months), but Humana, UHC and Anthem commercial publish no hard decision deadline. Contract disputes end in arbitration, not court (Humana AAA template with fee refund for winning groups under six physicians; Anthem fees split, confidential, interest capped at 5% simple; CareSource loser pays). Bulk routes: UHC Claims Research Project (20+ claims, same administrative issue); Anthem Availity up to 25 claims but same member only; Anthem IN Medicaid form for multiple like claims; CareSource systemic disputes (same reason, TIN, NPI); MHS groups similar claims at arbitration; Cigna says fee-schedule issues across patients need no individual appeals; Humana has none. Channel limits: UHC requires portal/API (no fax); Anthem expects Availity; fax is listed for Humana commercial and KY Medicaid, Aetna KY, CareSource IN, WellCare KY clinical/EIR, UHSS and MHS pre-arbitration. Not read: Passport 2026 manual (blocked), WellCare KY full manual (404), Cigna Reference Guide (login).

rules.citation: Humana 2026 Provider Manual for Physicians, Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (doc 773902ALL0725-A; PDF dated 2026-02-19), section 'Provider Claims Dispute Process', pp. 20-21
rules.quote: Claims disputes must be received by Humana within 18 months from the date the provider received notice of the original claim determination unless state or federal law or the agreement requires another time period or the claim will not be reopened.
rules.applies_to: Humana, ChoiceCare and HBHN participating providers, all products ('For all products'): Medicare Advantage and commercial (fully insured and self-funded Humana-administered); Medicaid follows the state manual where it differs.
rules.requires: Provider may dispute payment, denial or nonpayment (including denials caused by a denied authorization) via Availity (Claim Status > Dispute Claim > submit from Appeals worklist), phone 800-448-6262, or mail to Humana Correspondence, P.O. Box 14601, Lexington, KY 40512. A written request should include: provider name; NPI and TIN; member name and ID; date of service; relationship of subscriber to patient; claim number; charge; payment; proposed correct payment; difference; brief basis; supporting documentation.
rules.deadline: Received within 18 months from the date the provider received notice of the original claim determination (unless law or the agreement sets another period). The manual states no decision deadline for Humana.
rules.consequence: Late: 'the claim will not be reopened.' No interest or penalty is stated in the manual. Next step is the Escalated Review Process (HumanaProviderServices@humana.com, Provider Concierge Unit; auto-acknowledgement, reference ID within 3-5 business days), then the arbitration provisions of the provider agreement ('separate and distinct' from this process).
rules.provider_use: Put every listed data element in each fax/letter so it cannot be treated as incomplete; cite the 18-month window from the notice date; after a decision, escalate to the Provider Concierge Unit; a second dispute on the same encounter must 'explicitly identify specific new material information' ('Multiple provider dispute requests per provider encounter are generally unacceptable').

rules.citation: Humana Grievances and Appeals/Inquiry Directory (doc 954306ALL0226 (HUMP954306); PDF created 2026-07-21), 'Claim Payment Inquiries/Disputes', pp. 3-4
rules.quote: Look for an “Acknowledgment of Submission” email with a tracking number within 5 business days of your submission. Please allow 30 to 45 days from the date of the acknowledgment notice for our response.
rules.applies_to: Participating providers escalating a disagreement after Humana's first response (all lines).
rules.requires: Escalation by secure email to HumanaProviderServices@Humana.com with prior reference numbers, provider name and TIN, member ID and relationship, DOS, claim number, provider names, charge, actual payment, expected payment, basis for the contestation, and contact information.
rules.deadline: Humana's own stated targets: acknowledgment with tracking number within 5 business days; response 30 to 45 days from the acknowledgment ('Most inquiries receive a response in 30 to 45 days').
rules.consequence: These are service targets, not a contractual or legal deadline; the document attaches no consequence if Humana misses them.
rules.provider_use: Quote Humana's own 5-business-day acknowledgment and 30-45 day response targets in follow-up faxes, and use day 46 after acknowledgment as the trigger for the next escalation.

rules.citation: Humana Grievances and Appeals/Inquiry Directory (954306ALL0226), 'Medicare Advantage Grievances and Appeals', p. 5; Humana 2026 Provider Manual, 'Medicare Appeals Process', pp. 21-22
rules.quote: Participating providers do not have grievance and appeal rights on behalf of themselves, but they can appeal on behalf of their Humana-covered patients. Nonparticipating providers may appeal on behalf of themselves or on behalf of their Humana-covered patients.
rules.applies_to: Humana Medicare Advantage claims. Participating vs nonparticipating providers are treated differently.
rules.requires: Nonparticipating provider appeal: in writing with copy of claim, remittance showing denial, clinical support, and a signed Waiver of Liability Statement; mail Humana Grievance and Appeal Department, P.O. Box 14165, Lexington, KY 40512-4165, or Availity. Participating providers use the contractual dispute process (HUM-1), or appeal for the member with an Appointment of Representative.
rules.deadline: Nonparticipating: 'within 65 calendar days from the date of the denial notice'. Manual: post-service MA appeal decision '60 calendar days from the receipt of the request'.
rules.consequence: Late appeals are not accepted unless good cause (member). Upheld MA reconsiderations go to the CMS Independent Review Entity (process detail is in the medicare_advantage area).
rules.provider_use: For participating Humana MA claims, do not file a CMS-style reconsideration in the practice's own name; use the 18-month contractual dispute. For out-of-network MA claims, include the Waiver of Liability and file within 65 days.

rules.citation: Humana Physician Participation Agreement template, State: Kentucky (form 'HUM Phys 08-2006KY'), Article 13 'Grievance and Appeals Process/Binding Arbitration', sections 13.1-13.6; filed as Attachment I.C.18.d-3 to Kentucky MCO RFP #758 2000000202 (PDF 2019/2020)
rules.quote: The parties agree that any dispute arising out of their business relationship which cannot be settled by mutual agreement shall be submitted to final and binding arbitration under the Healthcare Payor Provider Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association (“AAA”)
rules.applies_to: Physicians contracted with Humana on this template (all products). The practice's signed agreement may differ; this is a template filed with the Commonwealth, not the practice's contract.
rules.requires: Exhaust Humana's internal review first (13.1); Medicare-appeal disputes go through the Medicare appeal process; one neutral arbitrator from the AAA National Healthcare Panel; venue within 50 miles of the physician's office; costs split equally; no joinder or class arbitration (13.4).
rules.deadline: None stated in the clause beyond prior exhaustion of internal review.
rules.consequence: Court suits on contract disputes are replaced by arbitration. For a physician practicing alone or in a group of fewer than six physicians, 'Humana agrees that it shall refund any applicable filing fees or arbitrators’ fees paid by such Physician in the event that Physician is the prevailing party'. A party that resists arbitration pays the other side's costs of compelling it (13.5).
rules.provider_use: The real escalation threat against Humana for contracted underpayments is a demand for AAA arbitration after internal exhaustion, not a lawsuit; check whether the practice's group size (fewer than six physicians) triggers the fee refund.

rules.citation: Humana Physician Participation Agreement template (Kentucky), section 15.3 (overpayment offsets)
rules.quote: Humana shall provide Physician thirty (30) days advance written notice of Humana’s intent to offset such amounts prior to deduction of any monies due.
rules.applies_to: Contracted physicians on this template.
rules.requires: Humana must give 30 days' advance written notice before offsetting an overpayment; physician may refund or request review within 30 days of the notice; retroactive adjustments limited to 18 months from original payment 'or such other period as may be required by applicable law'.
rules.deadline: Provider: request review within 30 days of the offset notice. Humana: no retroactive adjustment beyond 18 months from original payment.
rules.consequence: If the physician neither refunds nor requests review within 30 days, Humana may offset without further notice.
rules.provider_use: When RemitWatch sees a Humana takeback with no prior 30-day notice, or older than 18 months from the original payment, dispute it citing the agreement; always answer offset notices within 30 days.

rules.citation: Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky 2025 Provider Manual (572302KY1024; PDF created 2026-01-26), Chapter 7 'Provider grievance and appeals', 'Internal appeals', p. 53; network notice LC17925KY0722 (7/26/2022, effective 11/1/2022)
rules.quote: If a provider does not agree with the decision on a processed claim, the provider has 60 calendar days from the date of the original claim submission adjudication to file an appeal.
rules.applies_to: Providers serving Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky (Medicaid managed care), contracted and non-contracted.
rules.requires: Appeal in writing (Provider Grievance and Appeals, P.O. Box 14546, Lexington, KY 40512-4546), via Availity, by fax 800-949-2961, or by phone 800-444-9137 (per 2022 notice); say whether it is an inquiry, grievance or appeal.
rules.deadline: Provider: 60 calendar days from adjudication (the 2022 notice cites KRS 205.534(1)(d)). Humana: 'resolves provider grievances and appeals within 30 calendar days of receipt of the appeal request' and 'may request a 14-day extension'.
rules.consequence: Late: 'the claim is not considered and the appeal is denied.' After the internal appeal, the provider may request external independent review (HHH-KY-3).
rules.provider_use: Cite the 30-day resolution commitment in the appeal and calendar day 31 (day 45 if Humana took the extension) for follow-up and for starting the EIR clock.

rules.citation: Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky 2025 Provider Manual, 'Contracted rate dispute process', p. 88; Contracted Rate Dispute Form 366004KY1223-B (PDF 2025-08-05)
rules.quote: Humana Healthy Horizons determines and then mails the provider a dispute decision letter within 30 calendar days of receipt of a complete contracted rate dispute.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid providers with a contract or letter of agreement with Humana Healthy Horizons; disputes that the claim was not paid at the contracted rate (KRS 304.17A-708 per the manual).
rules.requires: Completed Contracted Rate Dispute Form plus the 'Explanation of Payment for the disputed claim(s)' and 'The contract provision that the provider believes was misapplied in paying the claim'. Submit by Availity, mail (Contracted Rate Disputes, P.O. Box 14546, Lexington, KY 40512-4546) or fax 800-949-2961.
rules.deadline: Provider: within 24 months of the original claim adjudication date. Humana: decision letter within 30 calendar days of a complete dispute.
rules.consequence: Humana 'may reject' a dispute that is incomplete, late, or missing requirements; the form says 'Incomplete submissions are rejected.'
rules.provider_use: For Humana KY Medicaid underpayments against the contract rate, use this 24-month route (far longer than the 60-day appeal) and always attach the EOP and quote the contract provision; the form's 'Expected outcome' field should state the dollar amount.

rules.citation: Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky 2025 Provider Manual, 'External independent reviews', pp. 54-56 (907 KAR 17:035)
rules.quote: The provider must submit a request for an EIR within 60 calendar days of receiving final decision on the internal appeal.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid managed care claims after Humana's internal appeal is exhausted. Excludes Medicare claims, SIU cases, incomplete forms, and 'Disputes based on reimbursement provisions or other provisions addressed in the proprietary agreement between the provider and the MCO'.
rules.requires: DMS EIR Intake Form only (verbal or other written requests not considered), every asterisked field complete, each issue and the basis of error stated; clock starts on electronic receipt, fax time stamp, or postmark plus 3 days.
rules.deadline: Provider: 60 calendar days. Humana: acknowledgment within 5 business days. EIR entity: final decision within 30 calendar days of receiving the packet. Administrative hearing request within 30 calendar days of the EIR decision.
rules.consequence: Losing party at the administrative hearing pays: 'The party that receives an adverse final order shall pay a fee not to exceed $1,000.' Either side may appeal the EIR decision.
rules.provider_use: A real, state-run third-party review the MCO cannot control, for coverage and claim-payment denials; mention in second-level letters that the practice will request EIR under 907 KAR 17:035 if the denial stands.

rules.citation: Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky 2025 Provider Manual, 'Claims compliance standards', p. 98; Anthem Kentucky Medicaid Provider Manual (KYBCBS-CD-PM-042746-23), claims chapter; Aetna Better Health of Kentucky 2026 Provider Manual, 'On-site Meeting', p. 101
rules.quote: As required by KRS § 205.534(1)(b), Humana Healthy Horizons extends each provider the opportunity for an in-person meeting with a Humana Healthy Horizons representative if a clean claim remains unpaid in violation of KRS § 304.17A-700 to KRS § 304.17A-730.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid MCOs (stated in the Humana, Anthem and Aetna KY Medicaid manuals).
rules.requires: MCO must offer an in-person meeting for a clean claim unpaid in violation of the KY prompt-pay statutes, and for any claim unpaid 45 or more days after receipt that 'individually, or in the aggregate, exceeds $2,500' (Anthem wording).
rules.deadline: Triggered when a claim is unpaid 45+ days after receipt and over $2,500 individually or in aggregate.
rules.consequence: The manuals state only the meeting right; statutory penalties and interest are in the kentucky area.
rules.provider_use: Aggregate small unpaid KY Medicaid claims per MCO until the total exceeds $2,500 and the oldest is 45+ days unpaid, then demand the in-person meeting in writing citing the MCO's own manual and KRS 205.534(1)(b). This is the one manual-backed lever that rewards bundling small dollars.

rules.citation: 2026 Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Kentucky Commercial Provider Manual (v1), effective September 1, 2026 (KY-BCBS-CM-PM-010987-26-S3103), 'Claim Payment Disputes', pp. 57-60; same text in 2026 Indiana Commercial Provider Manual v1 (eff. Aug 1, 2026) and v2 (eff. Jan 1, 2027)
rules.quote: Providers and Facilities have a minimum of two (2) years from the issue date of the EOP, unless otherwise required by State law (or such time period set forth in the Provider or Facility Agreement.
rules.applies_to: Anthem BCBS Kentucky and Indiana commercial and individual plans; participating providers and facilities (agreement may set other periods). Does not cover clinical/medical-necessity denials (separate clinical appeal).
rules.requires: Step 1 Claim Payment Reconsideration (phone, Availity, or writing; one per claim). Step 2 Claim Payment Appeal (Availity or writing) only after a reconsideration. Required documentation: position statement; provider name, address, phone, email, NPI or TIN; member name and Anthem ID; 'A listing of disputed Claims, which should include the Anthem Claim number and the date(s) of service(s)'; all supporting documentation. Mail: Anthem BCBS Payment Dispute Unit, P.O. Box 105557, Atlanta, GA 30348-5557.
rules.deadline: Reconsideration: within 2 years of the EOP issue date (KY says 'a minimum of'). Appeal: 'within ninety (90) days from the date of the determination of the Claims Payment Reconsideration'. No Anthem decision deadline is stated in the commercial manuals.
rules.consequence: Late without an extenuating circumstance: 'the request is deemed ineligible, and requests for payment will be denied', and the provider may not bill Anthem or the member. Both steps must be completed before the Agreement's dispute resolution and arbitration.
rules.provider_use: Two years is long enough to batch Anthem commercial underpayments; never let the 90-day appeal clock lapse after a reconsideration decision, because the appeal is the gateway to arbitration.

rules.citation: 2026 Anthem BCBS Kentucky Commercial Provider Manual, 'Dispute Resolution, Mediation, and Arbitration', sections A-H, pp. 13-16 (same in Indiana manuals)
rules.quote: pre-judgment interest shall be simple, not compounded, at an annual percentage rate no more than five percent (5%) or the interest applied for “clean claims”, whichever is less.
rules.applies_to: Contracted Anthem commercial providers whose Agreement has the dispute resolution and arbitration provisions (KY and IN).
rules.requires: Exhaust all administrative remedies; invoke dispute resolution by written notice with 'a detailed description of the dispute, all relevant underlying facts, a detailed description of the amount(s) in dispute and how they have been calculated'; monetary thresholds for meetings, mediation, arbitration panel and appeal are in the Agreement.
rules.deadline: Set by the Agreement (not stated in the manual).
rules.consequence: Neutral and administrative fees shared equally; each side pays its own attorneys; no consolidation across separate agreements; class-waiver disputes go to court; confidential proceedings; the state's statutory pre-judgment interest statute is agreed to be inapplicable.
rules.provider_use: Arbitration against Anthem is costly and interest-capped, so its value is as a credible step for pooled, documented underpayment patterns; the written notice must show the calculation per claim, which RemitWatch can generate.

rules.citation: Anthem Provider News - Kentucky, 'You can now submit one electronic claim dispute for multiple claims and access correspondence digitally, too', November 1, 2022 (KYBCBS-CM-10722-22-CPN10713); identical article in Anthem Provider News - Indiana, November 1, 2022
rules.quote: You can submit one dispute and add multiple claims — up to 25 claims — as long as the additional disputed claims are for the same member, provider, and dispute reason.
rules.applies_to: Anthem commercial member claims (KY and IN) disputed through Availity Essentials.
rules.requires: Same member, same provider, same dispute reason; maximum 25 claims per dispute.
rules.deadline: Same as ANT-COM-1.
rules.consequence: Each claim still produces its own correspondence (CI-COMM case number).
rules.provider_use: Bundle a patient's serial visits (e.g., staged Mohs, follow-ups) into one Availity dispute; cross-patient pattern underpayments are not covered by this bundle and belong in a pooled written dispute under the Agreement (ANT-COM-2).

rules.citation: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Provider Guidebook Medicare Advantage, January 1, 2027 (CR-PM-017345-26-GRP4605, dated November 1, 2026), sections 5.2-5.5.1, pp. 80-84
rules.quote: The plan will make every effort to resolve the claims payment reconsideration within 45 calendar days of receipt.
rules.applies_to: Anthem Medicare Advantage claims of contracted providers (Central region incl. IN and KY), payment and administrative disputes (not medical-necessity denials).
rules.requires: Reconsideration in writing, verbally or via Availity; then claim payment appeal via Availity or writing. Required: provider name, address, phone, email, NPI or TIN; member name and Medicare ID; 'A listing of disputed claims, which should include the claim number and the date(s) of service(s).'; supporting documentation. Mail (GA, IN, KY, MO, OH, WI): Anthem BCBS, ATTN: Medicare Payment Dispute Unit, P.O. Box 105187, Atlanta, GA 30348-5187.
rules.deadline: Provider: reconsideration within 120 calendar days of the EOP date; appeal within 30 calendar days of the reconsideration letter. Anthem: 'every effort' to resolve reconsideration within 45 calendar days and appeal within 30 calendar days of receipt.
rules.consequence: Late reconsiderations are 'untimely and denied unless good cause'; late appeals 'upheld unless good cause'. The determination letter must state the reason and support (statutes, policies, codes, manual references).
rules.provider_use: Track day 46 after a reconsideration and day 31 after an appeal and cite Anthem's own published turnaround in the follow-up; demand the specific policy or code support the guidebook says the letter must contain.

rules.citation: Anthem Medicare Advantage Provider Guidebook (Jan 1, 2027), section 2.18 'Prompt Payment by Medicare Advantage (MA) Organization' and section 7.2 'Nonparticipating Provider Appeals Rights'
rules.quote: Pay interest on clean claims not paid within 30 days
rules.applies_to: Noncontracted providers billing Anthem MA. Contracted providers: 'All contracted providers must include a prompt payment provision in their contract'.
rules.requires: Noncontracted: 95% of clean claims paid within 30 days; interest on clean claims not paid within 30 days; other claims approved or denied within 60 calendar days. Nonparticipating reconsideration of a denial with member liability: within 65 calendar days of the remittance notification with a signed Waiver of Liability, mailed to Medicare Complaints, Appeals and Grievances, Attention: Non-Contracted Provider Appeals, Mailstop OH0205-A537, 4361 Irwin Simpson Rd, Mason, OH 45040.
rules.deadline: 30 days (clean claims), 60 calendar days (other claims), 65 calendar days (nonpar reconsideration).
rules.consequence: Interest owed on late clean claims (rate and regulation are in the medicare_advantage area).
rules.provider_use: For out-of-network Anthem MA claims, check that interest was paid on clean claims paid after day 30 and demand it if missing.

rules.citation: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Medicaid, Provider Manual Kentucky Medicaid (KYBCBS-CD-PM-042746-23; PDF 2024-02-08), section 10.2.4 'Payment Appeals'
rules.quote: Payment appeals, whether verbal or written, must be received by Anthem within 90 calendar days of the remittance date.
rules.applies_to: Anthem Kentucky Medicaid managed care claims (contracted providers).
rules.requires: Verbal (855-661-2028) or written to Claim Appeals, Anthem, P.O. Box 62429, Virginia Beach, VA 23466-1599, or Availity Payment Appeal tool; 'a listing of disputed claims, a detailed explanation of the reason for the appeal', supporting documentation, copy of remit and the Kentucky universal MCO appeal form for written appeals.
rules.deadline: Provider: 90 calendar days of the remittance date. Anthem: 'Ensure a determination is made within 30 calendar days of the receipt of the payment appeal' (14-day extension; if the provider requests it, it is approved).
rules.consequence: Then external independent review (ANT-KYCAID-2). Section 10.2.5 ('Binding Arbitration') actually describes written negotiation: response within 30 days, principals meet within 30 days of the response, then 'all available remedies at law or equity'.
rules.provider_use: Cite the 30-day determination standard; for disputes under the agreement, send the certified-mail written description with a proposed resolution and deadline, which obliges a written response within 30 days.

rules.citation: Anthem Kentucky Medicaid Provider Manual, section 10.3.2 'External Review and Administrative Hearing for the Provider' (907 KAR 17:035; 907 KAR 17:040)
rules.quote: If the external review decision is to overturn the original Anthem decision, the claim will be adjusted within 30 days of the decision.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid claims after Anthem's internal appeal; dates of service on or after 12/1/2016.
rules.requires: Written request (not verbal) by email KYExternalReview@anthem.com, fax 502-212-7336, mail Central Appeals Processing P.O. Box 62429, or Availity; identify each issue, state why Anthem's decision is wrong, give contact details, mark 'External Independent Review'.
rules.deadline: Provider: 60 calendar days from receipt of Anthem's final internal decision (receipt rules incl. postmark plus 3 days). Anthem: acknowledgment within 5 business days; to DMS within 15 business days; decision within 30 days (45 business days if extended); claim adjusted within 30 days of an overturn. Administrative hearing within 30 calendar days of the decision.
rules.consequence: Party with an adverse final order 'shall pay a fee of $600 to DMS for the cost of the Administrative Hearing' (figure differs from Humana's manual; see open questions).
rules.provider_use: State the EIR route and the 30-day payment-after-overturn duty in second-level KY Medicaid letters.

rules.citation: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Indiana Medicaid Provider Manual (HHW, HIP, HCC, PathWays) INBCBS-CD-PM-070775-24 (PDF 2025-04-09), 'Informal Claim Disputes' and 'Formal Appeals', pp. 150-152
rules.quote: Anthem will make every effort to resolve the formal appeal within 45 calendar days of receipt. If a determination is not made within 45 days, the decision will be rendered in favor of the provider.
rules.applies_to: Anthem Indiana Medicaid managed care (Hoosier Healthwise, HIP, Hoosier Care Connect, Indiana PathWays for Aging) claims.
rules.requires: Informal dispute (writing, phone or Availity) then formal appeal (Availity or writing with the Provider Dispute Resolution Request form) to Provider Disputes and Appeals, P.O. Box 61599, Virginia Beach, VA 23466-1599; listing of disputed claims with claim numbers and dates of service; supporting documentation.
rules.deadline: Informal: within 60 calendar days of the EOP date; Anthem resolves within 30 calendar days (+30 with written extension letter). Formal appeal: within 60 calendar days of the reconsideration letter; 45 calendar days to decide.
rules.consequence: No decision within 45 days on a formal appeal: 'the decision will be rendered in favor of the provider.' Then binding arbitration per the provider agreement. Late filings denied unless good cause (manual lists good-cause categories). If Anthem asks for information, the provider must return it within 21 days or the case may close.
rules.provider_use: The strongest lever in Anthem's manuals: every formal appeal letter should state the receipt date and that, under Anthem's own manual, no decision within 45 days means the appeal is decided for the practice; RemitWatch should then demand payment on day 46.

rules.citation: Anthem BCBS Indiana Provider Dispute Resolution Request Form (WEBPAIN-0226-17, June 2017), pages 1-2
rules.quote: Use this page only for multiple like claims (disputed for the same reason).
rules.applies_to: Anthem Indiana Medicaid (HHW, HIP, HCC) disputes.
rules.requires: Check 'Substantially similar multiple claims' and list each claim (patient, health plan ID, claim ID, service dates) on page 2; required fields marked with asterisks.
rules.deadline: As ANT-INCAID-1.
rules.consequence: 'Submission of this form constitutes agreement not to bill the patient during the dispute process.'
rules.provider_use: One faxable/mailed dispute can carry many like claims across different patients for Anthem Indiana Medicaid.

rules.citation: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide for Commercial, Individual Exchange and Medicare Advantage (PDF 2026-05-13), Chapter 10, section 5 'Claim reconsideration and appeals process', pp. 133-135; guide effective April 1, 2026 for current contracts (Jan 1, 2026 for contracts on or after that date)
rules.quote: You must submit your reconsideration and appeal to us within 12 months from the date of the original claim EOB or PRA (or as required by law or your Agreement).
rules.applies_to: UnitedHealthcare commercial, Individual Exchange and Medicare Advantage network (contracted) providers; non-network MA providers follow the separate Medicare non-contracted dispute process; does not apply in some states (CA, OR, WA listed).
rules.requires: Step 1 claim reconsideration, Step 2 appeal, both through the UnitedHealthcare Provider Portal (Claims & Payments) or API; appeal must attach all new supporting materials and not repeat reconsideration materials.
rules.deadline: 12 months total from the original EOB/PRA for both steps. No UnitedHealthcare decision deadline is stated in Chapter 10.
rules.consequence: Outcome shown by updated EOB/PRA or a letter where required by law; after the appeal, only the Agreement's dispute resolution remains (UHC-3).
rules.provider_use: Because the 12 months covers both steps, file the reconsideration early enough to leave room for the appeal and the Notice of Dispute; RemitWatch should compute one UHC clock from the original PRA date.

rules.citation: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide, Chapter 1 'Obligation to do business with UnitedHealthcare electronically', p. 5; Chapter 10 '20 or more claim reconsiderations (research request)', p. 134; UHCprovider.com 'Pre- and post-service appeals and reconsiderations' page (fetched 2026-11-23)
rules.quote: If you have a request to reconsider 20 or more paid or denied claims for the same administrative issue (and attachments are not required), you may submit these in bulk online.
rules.applies_to: UnitedHealthcare network providers (commercial, Individual Exchange, MA; the web page also names Community Plan).
rules.requires: Bulk: UHCprovider.com > Sign In > Claims & Payments > Claims Research Project (20+ claims, same administrative issue, no attachments). Contract set-up or bulk payment problems: claim research project or provider advocate. Channel: 'where allowed by law, UnitedHealthcare requires you to use digital tools where available ... This includes submissions and inquiries related to claims, reconsiderations and appeals'. The Single Paper Claim Reconsideration form is only for when electronic submission is not possible: 'This form is for submitting 1 claim at a time, not for bulk or multiple claims.' (mail to the PRA address; no fax).
rules.deadline: Same 12-month window (UHC-1).
rules.consequence: Fax is not a listed channel for UHC network reconsiderations or appeals; non-digital submissions risk being treated as non-compliant with the guide.
rules.provider_use: Route UHC work through the portal or UHC's API (Reconsiderations and appeals are API-enabled), and pool 20+ same-issue claims into one Claims Research Project instead of faxing.

rules.citation: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide, Chapter 10 'Resolving potential reimbursement issues' and 'Arbitration locations', pp. 145-146
rules.quote: Unless your Agreement prescribes a different time frame, a Notice of Dispute must be sent no later than 60 days after the date of our decision on your appeal.
rules.applies_to: UnitedHealthcare contracted providers (commercial, Individual Exchange, MA).
rules.requires: Notice of Dispute sent per the Agreement's notice method and address, stating that dispute resolution is being initiated ('Notice of Dispute' in the reference line), with per-claim fields: group number, subscriber number, patient name and DOB, TIN, first and last DOS, billed charges, units, UHC payment, patient responsibility, contractual reimbursement expected, balance due, account number, detailed basis, CPT/HCPCS, reference numbers, reconsideration and appeal dates and reference numbers.
rules.deadline: 60 days after the appeal decision (unless the Agreement differs).
rules.consequence: 'Failure to timely comply with this process and the requirements in your Agreement will result in the waiver of your right to initiate dispute resolution and waiver of your right to pursue such claim or issue in any forum.' Arbitration venue unless the Agreement differs: Marion County, IN (Indiana care) and Fayette County, KY (Kentucky care).
rules.provider_use: This is the step that preserves every later remedy against UHC: RemitWatch should auto-generate the Notice of Dispute (it already holds most fields) within 60 days of each upheld appeal worth pursuing.

rules.citation: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide, Chapter 10 'Disagreement' (overpayments), p. 133
rules.quote: you may submit a notice of disagreement within 30 calendar days (or as required by law or your Agreement) from the date of receipt of notification.
rules.applies_to: UnitedHealthcare network providers receiving an overpayment refund request or adjustment.
rules.requires: Clearly state the basis for disagreement and include supporting documentation, following the instructions in the notification.
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days from receipt of the overpayment notification.
rules.consequence: Not stated in the guide (the notification controls); missing the window lets the adjustment stand.
rules.provider_use: Track UHC takeback notices and answer within 30 days.

rules.citation: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide, 'UMR and UHSS supplement' (Applicability; Claim reconsideration and appeals process; FAQ), pp. 417-423; contact table p. 149
rules.quote: You are subject to both the UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide and this supplement. This supplement supersedes the main guide if there is conflicting information.
rules.applies_to: UMR (UHC's third-party administrator for self-funded employer plans) and UnitedHealthcare Shared Services claims where the practice is in a UnitedHealthcare network.
rules.requires: Claim Reconsideration Request Form with member name and ID, DOS/claim information, provider name, address and TIN, and all supporting materials; submit via UMR.com (Find your claim > Appeal/review this claim), mail UMR - Claim Appeals, P.O. Box 30546, Salt Lake City, UT 84130-0546 (or RA address), or phone. UHSS post-service: fax 1-866-427-7703 or P.O. Box 30783, Salt Lake City, UT 84130-0783.
rules.deadline: The supplement sets no separate window, so the main guide's 12 months (UHC-1) is the contractual outer limit (my reading); 'Timely filing requirements are determined by the self-funded customer, as well as the provider-contracted timely filing provisions.' Member-level appeal deadlines come from the plan document.
rules.consequence: Overpayments: refund within 30 calendar days or UMR offsets; recoupment attempted for 120 days then referred to Payment Resolution Solutions.
rules.provider_use: Use the UHC network contract (12 months, Notice of Dispute) for UMR underpayments; for benefit denials, appeal under the plan document on the member's behalf with authorization. State prompt-pay leverage is generally not available against self-funded plans (see does_not_apply).

rules.citation: Cigna Healthcare, 'Appeals and Disputes Policy and Procedures' provider web page (cigna.com, ©2026; fetched 2026-11-23), 'How to Submit an Appeal'
rules.quote: The review will be completed in 60 days and the health care provider will receive notification of the dispute resolution within 75 business days of receipt of the original dispute.
rules.applies_to: Cigna Healthcare commercial post-service payment disputes and claim denials by contracted providers ('Processes may vary due to state mandates or contract provisions'; California differs).
rules.requires: Call Customer Service (1-800-882-4462) first; then the Request for Health Care Provider Payment Review form 'fully completed' with the original EOB/EOP or information request letter and supporting documentation, mailed to Cigna Healthcare Inc. National Appeals Unit (NAO), PO Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422 (PO Box 188062 for 'GWH-Cigna' or 'G' ID cards). Claim-coding-edit denials can also be sent as a reconsideration through CignaforHCP.
rules.deadline: Provider: 'within 180 calendar days of the date of the initial payment or denial notice' or of the last payment adjustment. Cigna: review completed in 60 days; notice within 75 business days. 'Time periods are subject to applicable law and the health care provider agreement.'
rules.consequence: If no timely internal appeal or arbitration request, 'the last Cigna Healthcare determination will be final' and 'Customers cannot be billed for any amount denied because you failed to submit the request for review or arbitration within the required timelines.'
rules.provider_use: Cite Cigna's own 60-day review commitment and 75-business-day notice in follow-ups; mail with tracking because no provider-appeal fax is published.

rules.citation: Cigna Healthcare 'Appeals and Disputes Policy and Procedures' page, 'Arbitration'
rules.quote: With respect to health care provider payment or termination disputes, you must request arbitration within one year of the date of the letter communicating the final internal level review decision.
rules.applies_to: Cigna contracted providers (agreement's arbitration clause controls if present; otherwise the page's default applies).
rules.requires: Written notice to the other party; without an agreement clause, a Request for a Dispute Resolution List to the American Health Lawyers Association ADR Service with the administrative fee.
rules.deadline: One year from the final internal decision letter.
rules.consequence: 'Arbitration will be the exclusive remedy'; binding; no consolidation or class basis; the agreement stays in force.
rules.provider_use: Calendar the one-year arbitration window from each upheld Cigna appeal letter; pooled underpayments can justify one AHLA arbitration per agreement.

rules.citation: Cigna 'Request for Health Care Professional Payment Review' form (PDF modified 2021-08-16), header notes and Step 2
rules.quote: Fee schedule or reimbursement terms for multiple patients do not require individual appeals.
rules.applies_to: Cigna commercial contracted professionals.
rules.requires: Fee-schedule problems across patients go to Customer Service, or to the Experience Manager/Experience Consultant if the contract is being misapplied; single-claim appeals use the form or a letter marked 'Health Care Professional Appeal' with the original claim and EOP/EOB.
rules.deadline: 'Your appeal should be submitted within 180 days and allow 60 days for processing your appeal, unless other timelines are required by state law.'
rules.consequence: Not stated on the form.
rules.provider_use: Send Cigna fee-schedule underpayment patterns as one pooled contract-misapplication notice to the Experience Manager instead of claim-by-claim appeals.

rules.citation: WellCare of Kentucky Medicaid Provider Quick Reference Guide 2026 (PDF 2026-04-17), 'Claim Payment Appeals', 'Claim Payment Policy Disputes', 'Recovery/Cost Containment Unit', 'Clinical Appeals', 'KY External Review Process', pp. 2-5
rules.quote: Claim payment appeals must be submitted in writing to WellCare within 24 months of the date on the EOP.
rules.applies_to: WellCare of Kentucky Medicaid managed care claims.
rules.requires: Claim payment appeals (timely filing, incidental, unlisted, non-covered codes) with all supporting documentation via provider.wellcare.com or mail WellCare of Kentucky, Attn: Claim Payment Appeals, P.O. Box 31370, Tampa, FL 33631-3370. Authorization/medical-necessity denials go to the Appeals Department (fax 1-866-201-0657). Overpayment administrative review by mail or fax 1-877-277-1805. EIR by fax 1-800-509-8203 or Kyexternalreview@wellcare.com.
rules.deadline: Claim payment and payment-policy appeals: 24 months from the EOP date. Clinical appeals: 60 calendar days of the denial. Overpayment administrative review: 60 days from the letter; 'A Final Determination will be rendered within 30 days of the date of WellCare’s receipt of your request.' EIR: 60 days from receipt of the notice.
rules.consequence: Overpayment review: documents sent after the initial request 'will not be considered'. WellCare's decision time for claim payment appeals is not stated in the guide.
rules.provider_use: Use the 24-month window to pool WellCare payment appeals; send the complete packet the first time because late documents are ignored in overpayment reviews.

rules.citation: Aetna Better Health of Kentucky 2026 Provider Manual (Aetna/2350 10-01-25 (1/26); PDF modified 2026-08-07), 'Appeal Process for Providers' and 'Resolution of the Appeal', pp. 107-108
rules.quote: We must receive your appeal within one (1) year of the incident, remit date or date of notice of action that caused the appeal. We will respond to your appeal in writing within thirty (30) calendar days of when we receive it.
rules.applies_to: Aetna Better Health of Kentucky Medicaid providers (907 KAR 17:015): denied claims, claims 'not acted upon within a reasonable time', and contractual disputes.
rules.requires: Written appeal letter with supporting documentation to Attn: KY Appeals & Grievances, PO Box 81040, 5801 Postal Rd, Cleveland, OH 44181; the web page also lists secure fax 1-855-454-5585 ('the fastest and best way'), email KYAppealandGrievance@aetna.com, phone, and the provider portal.
rules.deadline: Provider: one year per the manual, but the web page says 'You can file an appeal within 60 days of receiving a Notice of Action' (conflict). Aetna: acknowledgment within 5 business days; decision within 30 calendar days; 14-day extension only if it benefits the provider.
rules.consequence: Then external independent review (60 calendar days; fax 1-844-359-6670, AetnaExternalReview@aetna.com) and administrative hearing; 'If the provider prevails in the external appeal, we will comply with the Final Order within sixty (60) days'.
rules.provider_use: File within 60 days to be safe despite the manual's one year; cite the 30-day decision duty and the 'not acted upon within a reasonable time' ground for unanswered claims.

rules.citation: Aetna Better Health of Kentucky 2026 Provider Manual, 'Recoveries', pp. 100-101
rules.quote: In such an instance, Aetna Better Health shall not proceed with the recoupment until the dispute is resolved.
rules.applies_to: Aetna Better Health of Kentucky overpayment recoveries.
rules.requires: Aetna may seek recovery up to 24 months after the first remittance date (longer for fraud); notice must give amount, member, DOS, claim reference and basis; provider may send a notice of disagreement within 30 days of postmark/electronic delivery.
rules.deadline: Provider: 30 days. Aetna: disputes resolved within 30 calendar days through the provider appeals process.
rules.consequence: Timely disagreement stops recoupment until resolved. The manual also says clean claims not adjudicated in time 'shall be paid with interest, in accordance with Commonwealth of Kentucky statute.'
rules.provider_use: Answer every Aetna KY recovery notice within 30 days to freeze the offset; reject recoveries older than 24 months.

rules.citation: Passport by Molina Healthcare 2026 Kentucky Medicaid Provider Manual (DMS approved; 'Last Updated: 11/2025' per search excerpt), claims/appeals sections
rules.quote: (not read) Search-engine excerpt only: provider appeals may be submitted via 'Availity.com (preferred submission)' and fax '(866) 315-2572'.
rules.applies_to: Passport by Molina Healthcare (Kentucky Medicaid managed care).
rules.requires: Not confirmed. A 2022 Passport presentation (secondary) said 60 calendar days from the adverse determination; a 2022 appeal form reportedly said incomplete forms are returned unprocessed.
rules.deadline: Unconfirmed.
rules.consequence: Unconfirmed. The EIR rules of 907 KAR 17:035 apply to all KY Medicaid MCOs (kentucky area).
rules.provider_use: Do not automate Passport deadlines from this entry; obtain the manual by hand from the Passport provider site before faxing.

rules.citation: MHS (Managed Health Services) Indiana Provider Manual (code 0126.PR.P.JB; PDF modified 2026-02-09), Chapter 5 'Claims Administrative Reviews and Appeals': 'Informal Claim Dispute' and 'Formal Claim Dispute - Administrative Claim Appeal', pp. 25-27
rules.quote: In the event MHS fails to deliver to the provider a written determination within 45 calendar days of the initial receipt of the administrative claim appeal, the initial decision will be overturned and the appeal ruled in favor of the provider.
rules.applies_to: MHS Indiana Medicaid claims (contracted and non-contracted providers per the arbitration section); not medical-necessity appeals.
rules.requires: Level 1 informal dispute via Secure Provider Portal or in writing (EOP plus informal dispute form, or letterhead letter) identifying the claim(s) and the reason; mail Managed Health Services, P.O. Box 3002, Farmington, MO 63640 (medical). Level 2 administrative claim appeal in writing on letterhead with 'appeal' clearly marked, same address; only after a Level 1 dispute.
rules.deadline: Level 1: within 60 calendar days from the EOP date; MHS responds within 30 calendar days. Level 2: within 60 calendar days of receiving the informal resolution notice; acknowledgment within 5 business days; written determination within 45 calendar days. Claims processed within 30 calendar days after a final determination.
rules.consequence: No Level 2 decision within 45 days: the denial is overturned and the claim reprocessed. Phone calls or the portal 'online reconsideration' do not stop the 60-day clock: 'It will not stop the 60-calendar-day count from the date of your EOP to file a written informal dispute or appeal.'
rules.provider_use: Every Level 2 letter should say 'APPEAL', give the receipt date, and quote the 45-day overturn rule; on day 46 RemitWatch should demand reprocessing in writing.

rules.citation: MHS Indiana Provider Manual, Chapter 5 'Arbitration', p. 27 (405 IAC 1-1.6-1 et seq.)
rules.quote: Claims with similar issues from the same provider may be grouped together for the purpose of requesting arbitration.
rules.applies_to: MHS Indiana Medicaid, contracted and non-contracted providers, after the administrative claim appeal.
rules.requires: Written pre-arbitration request on letterhead, explaining why the claims should be paid and showing they went through both prior levels; mail MHS Pre-Arbitration Review, 429 N. Pennsylvania Street, Suite 109, Indianapolis, IN 46204, or fax 1 (833) 364-2498.
rules.deadline: Request 'postmarked no later than 60 calendar days after the date the provider received MHS’ decision on the administrative claim appeal'; MHS assigns staff to research within 30 calendar days and responds with information or a settlement offer.
rules.consequence: Binding arbitration under American Health Lawyers Association rules and the Indiana Uniform Arbitration Act (IC 34-57-2-1 et seq.) unless both agree otherwise.
rules.provider_use: Group all small MHS denials with the same issue into one pre-arbitration request, which by the manual triggers a review and possible settlement within 30 days.

rules.citation: CareSource Indiana Medicaid Provider Manual (Hoosier Healthwise, Healthy Indiana Plan; PDF 2025-04-23), 'Provider Grievances, Claim Disputes & Appeals Process', pp. 112-114; CareSource Indiana Medicaid 'Provider Disputes or Appeals' web page (fetched 2026-11-23)
rules.quote: CareSource must issue a written decision within 45 days of receipt of the written request for appeal. If the appeal is not resolved within the 45-day time frame, the appeal will be determined as an approval.
rules.applies_to: CareSource Indiana Medicaid, participating and nonparticipating providers.
rules.requires: Claim dispute first (portal preferred; verbal; or written dispute form by fax (937) 531-2398 or mail Claim Disputes Department, P.O. Box 2008, Dayton, OH 45401-2008); then claim appeal (portal or Provider Claim Appeal Request Form, mail Attn: Provider Appeals, same P.O. Box, fax 937-531-2398) with member name and ID, provider name and ID, codes and reason. 'Claims appeals filed without first submitting a dispute will not be processed.'
rules.deadline: Dispute: 'within 60 days after the provider’s receipt of the written determination of the claim'; 'If CareSource fails to decision a claim within 30 days after receipt, an appeal may be submitted.' Appeal: within 60 days of the dispute resolution; decision within 45 days.
rules.consequence: No appeal decision in 45 days: 'the appeal will be determined as an approval.'
rules.provider_use: Fax disputes and appeals (fax is a listed channel); if no dispute answer in 30 days, appeal immediately; then hold CareSource to day 45.

rules.citation: CareSource Indiana Medicaid Provider Manual, 'Arbitration', p. 114 (IC 34-57-2)
rules.quote: The fees and expenses of arbitration or other binding resolution procedure shall be borne by the non-prevailing party.
rules.applies_to: CareSource Indiana Medicaid providers dissatisfied with the appeal panel decision.
rules.requires: Submit under the agreement's dispute resolution provisions to CareSource, Attn: Arbitration, 251 N Illinois Street, Suite 300, Indianapolis, IN 46204; AHLA rules under the Indiana Uniform Arbitration Act unless agreed otherwise or statute imposes another procedure.
rules.deadline: Not stated in the manual.
rules.consequence: Loser pays arbitration fees and expenses; 'The arbitration process may include, in a single arbitration proceeding, matters from multiple formal claim resolution procedures'.
rules.provider_use: Loser-pays plus consolidation makes pooled, well-documented CareSource claims a credible arbitration threat; weak claims carry fee risk.

rules.citation: CareSource network notification IN-MED-P-488869 'Dispute and Appeal Clarification' (July 2, 2021; OMPP approved 06/24/2021)
rules.quote: If a systemic issue is identified, multiple claims may be submitted for one dispute. When submitting multiple claims, the claims must be disputed for the same reason and under the same Tax ID and NPI.
rules.applies_to: CareSource Indiana Medicaid providers.
rules.requires: A completed appeal and dispute form with the claims; separate disputes for different issues; detailed explanation of why the claims are disputed.
rules.deadline: Informal dispute within 60 calendar days of receipt of the EOP; if unresolved within 30 days, formal appeal within 60 days after the end of that 30-day period.
rules.consequence: 'It is not recommended to submit a generic or a copied form, this may delay the response or result in the dispute or appeal not being processed.'
rules.provider_use: Group same-reason CareSource claims under one TIN/NPI per dispute, but generate a claim-specific explanation rather than boilerplate.

rules.citation: Humana Healthy Horizons in Indiana claim-payment inquiry resolution guide for Indiana PathWays for Aging providers (567406IN0924; PDF 2025-01-08), pp. 1-2
rules.quote: If you are a participating provider and disagree with our determination after we respond to your informal claim dispute, you can email a claim appeal to IndianaFormalDispute@humana.com
rules.applies_to: Humana Healthy Horizons in Indiana (Indiana PathWays for Aging Medicaid managed care) providers.
rules.requires: Informal dispute via Availity, email INMedicaidClaimsResearch@humana.com, or mail (Informal Claim Dispute, P.O. Box 14169, Lexington, KY 40512-4169) with TIN, Medicaid ID, DOS, claim number, etc.; formal dispute/claim appeal by email or mail to Attn: Formal Claim Appeals, 201 N. Illinois St., Suite 1200, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
rules.deadline: Not stated in this guide ('Most inquiries receive a response in 30 to 45 days'); Indiana MCO timelines are in the indiana area.
rules.consequence: Not stated in this guide.
rules.provider_use: PathWays is an aging program, so it may matter to a skin-cancer practice; confirm filing windows before automating.

batch_and_channel: Humana (MA, commercial): Availity Claim Status > Dispute Claim > Appeals worklist (one claim at a time; no bulk dispute route found); phone 800-448-6262; mail Humana Correspondence, P.O. Box 14601, Lexington, KY 40512. Commercial standard appeal fax 888-556-2128 (2023 guide). Manual: 'Multiple provider dispute requests per provider encounter are generally unacceptable.' Escalation: HumanaProviderServices@humana.com (secure email). PPI medical-record disputes fax 888-815-8912. Online tool cannot be used for overpayment/PPI disputes.

Humana Healthy Horizons KY (Medicaid): Availity, fax 800-949-2961, mail P.O. Box 14546 (appeals, contracted rate disputes) / P.O. Box 14601 (claim disputes), phone 800-444-9137; contract-rate dispute form allows 'Explanation of Payment for the disputed claim(s)' but requires the misapplied contract provision; EIR only on the DMS EIR Intake Form.

Anthem commercial KY/IN: Availity Claim Status dispute is the expected channel ('It is the expectation of Anthem that electronic Claim payment disputes are adopted'); phone; mail Payment Dispute Unit, P.O. Box 105557, Atlanta, GA 30348-5557. Bundle: up to 25 claims per Availity dispute only for the same member, provider and dispute reason. Required documentation includes 'A listing of disputed Claims'. No fax listed.

Anthem Medicare Advantage (IN, KY): Availity Dispute Claim, verbal (reconsideration only), or mail Medicare Payment Dispute Unit, P.O. Box 105187, Atlanta, GA 30348-5187 with the Reconsideration or Claim Payment Appeal Form; 'A listing of disputed claims' required. Nonpar appeals: mail to Mason, OH address with Waiver of Liability.

Anthem KY Medicaid: verbal (855-661-2028), Availity Payment Appeal tool, or mail Claim Appeals, P.O. Box 62429, Virginia Beach, VA; 'listing of disputed claims' accepted; EIR by email KYExternalReview@anthem.com or fax 502-212-7336.

Anthem IN Medicaid: Availity, verbal (informal only), or mail Provider Disputes and Appeals, P.O. Box 61599, Virginia Beach, VA 23466-1599 with the Provider Dispute Resolution Request Form, whose page 2 lists 'multiple like claims (disputed for the same reason)' across patients.

UnitedHealthcare (commercial, Exchange, MA): portal or API only for network providers ('requires you to use digital tools where available'); bulk = Claims Research Project for 20+ paid/denied claims with the same administrative issue and no attachments; paper Single Paper Claim Reconsideration form only when electronic is impossible, one claim per form, mailed to the PRA address; no fax. Notice of Dispute goes to the Agreement's notice address.

UMR: UMR.com 'Appeal/review this claim', mail UMR - Claim Appeals, P.O. Box 30546, Salt Lake City, UT 84130-0546 (or RA address), or phone; no post-service fax listed in the 2026 guide (an older 2016 form listed fax 877-291-3248; treat as outdated). UHSS post-service fax 1-866-427-7703.

Cigna commercial: call 1-800-882-4462 first; mail the Payment Review form to National Appeals Unit, PO Box 188011 (or 188062 for GWH/G cards), Chattanooga, TN 37422; no provider-appeal fax published; claim-coding-edit reconsiderations through CignaforHCP; fee-schedule problems across many patients go to Customer Service or the Experience Manager without individual appeals.

WellCare KY: provider.wellcare.com or mail (Claim Payment Appeals P.O. Box 31370, Tampa, FL); clinical appeals fax 1-866-201-0657; overpayment review fax 1-877-277-1805; EIR fax 1-800-509-8203; paper claims cannot be faxed.
Aetna Better Health KY: secure fax 1-855-454-5585 (Aetna calls it the fastest), email KYAppealandGrievance@aetna.com, portal, phone, or mail PO Box 81040, Cleveland, OH 44181; EIR fax 1-844-359-6670.
Passport by Molina (KY): Availity preferred and fax (866) 315-2572 per search excerpt only (unconfirmed).

MHS (IN): Secure Provider Portal or mail P.O. Box 3002, Farmington, MO 63640 for Level 1 and Level 2; Level 2 must be a letterhead letter marked 'appeal'; pre-arbitration fax 1 (833) 364-2498; similar claims may be grouped for arbitration; phone and portal 'online reconsideration' do not stop the 60-day clock.

CareSource (IN): portal (preferred), verbal, fax (937) 531-2398, or mail P.O. Box 2008, Dayton, OH 45401; multiple claims allowed in one dispute for a systemic issue if same reason, Tax ID and NPI; arbitration may combine multiple formal claim resolution matters.

Humana Healthy Horizons IN (PathWays): Availity, email INMedicaidClaimsResearch@humana.com (informal), IndianaFormalDispute@humana.com (formal), or mail; PPI multi-claim issues use the PPI Issue Resolution Team Escalation Submission Form.
does_not_apply: Humana MA: the manual says 'State laws and/or regulations do not affect the adjudication of claims for Medicare Advantage members' (2026 Provider Manual p. 4), so Kentucky/Indiana prompt-pay and dispute statutes are not the lever for Humana MA claims; contracted MA payment disputes run through the 18-month contractual dispute, not the CMS member appeal track ('Participating providers do not have grievance and appeal rights on behalf of themselves').

Kentucky Medicaid external independent review (907 KAR 17:035) does not cover Medicare claims, cases where MCO internal appeals were not exhausted, SIU/fraud cases, incomplete forms, or 'Disputes based on reimbursement provisions or other provisions addressed in the proprietary agreement between the provider and the MCO' (Humana KY manual); contract-rate disputes use the MCO's contracted rate dispute process instead.

UMR/UHSS self-funded plans: UMR 'is not an insurance company'; timely filing is set by the self-funded customer and the provider contract. Kentucky and Indiana insurance prompt-pay laws generally cannot be enforced against self-funded ERISA plans (ERISA preemption); that legal conclusion belongs to the erisa_commercial area and was not verified here.

Anthem commercial arbitration: the manual states providers 'agree that the state’s statutory pre-judgment interest statute is inapplicable to Dispute Resolution and Arbitration' (interest capped at 5% simple or the clean-claim rate, whichever is less); arbitrators cannot consolidate separately filed arbitrations or separate provider agreements.
Anthem's Availity 25-claim bundle does not cover claims for different members; UHC's paper reconsideration form cannot carry multiple claims; Humana publishes no bulk dispute route.

Fax is not an accepted channel for UnitedHealthcare network reconsiderations/appeals (digital obligation) and is not listed for Anthem commercial/MA payment disputes, Cigna provider appeals, or UMR post-service appeals.

Cigna: only one internal provider appeal level is described; the Independent Review Organization route is offered only for certain customer (member) appeals such as medical necessity, with the patient's approval, not for contract payment disputes.

Payer manuals do not make litigation the remedy for contracted providers: Humana (AAA), Anthem (Agreement arbitration), UHC (Notice of Dispute then Agreement arbitration), Cigna (arbitration as exclusive remedy), MHS and CareSource (AHLA binding arbitration) all route contract disputes to arbitration, mostly confidential and without class or consolidation (CareSource allows combining multiple claim matters).
open_questions: Passport by Molina 2026 KY Medicaid manual could not be downloaded (bot block/404 on 2026-11-23); its dispute deadlines, decision times and fax number are unconfirmed.
WellCare of Kentucky full provider manual URLs returned 404; WellCare's decision timeframe for claim payment appeals is not stated in the 2026 Quick Reference Guide.
Aetna Better Health KY: manual says appeals within one year; the web page says within 60 days of a Notice of Action. Which controls?

Kentucky Medicaid appeal windows differ by MCO (Humana 60 days citing KRS 205.534(1)(d); Anthem 90 days; Aetna 1 year/60 days; WellCare 24 months for claim payment appeals); the kentucky area should confirm the statutory minimum.
Kentucky administrative hearing fee after EIR: Humana manual says 'not to exceed $1,000'; Anthem manual says '$600'. Check 907 KAR 17:040.
Anthem Kentucky Medicaid manual found is dated February 2024 (KYBCBS-CD-PM-042746-23); a newer edition may exist.

The practice's signed Humana, Anthem, UHC and Cigna agreements were not available; arbitration rules, monetary thresholds, notice addresses and any shorter dispute windows in those agreements control over the manuals.
Humana's 18-month window runs from when the provider 'received notice' of the determination; RemitWatch needs the 835/EOP receipt date, not only the check date.
No published decision deadline was found for Humana, UHC or Anthem commercial contracted-provider disputes; state prompt-pay statutes (kentucky/indiana areas) may supply one.

Indiana deemed-approval rules (Anthem IN Medicaid, MHS, CareSource at 45 days) appear in all three manuals; the indiana area should confirm the underlying rule (405 IAC 1-1.6 or the IHCP MCO contract).
Cigna's full Reference Guide is behind the CignaforHCP login and was not read; Cigna's reconsideration (portal) timeframe is unconfirmed.
Whether Anthem's 25-claim Availity bundle (announced Nov 2022) is still live in 2026 was not re-confirmed in the 2026 manuals.
Humana Healthy Horizons in Indiana filing deadlines are not printed in the 2025 guide.
